from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Generalization to Parabola and Hyperbola", [
            "Adjusting the plane slope changes the conic shape.",
            "The parabola moves one sphere to infinity.",
            "The hyperbola sphere moves to the other nap."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=3).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT).set_opacity(0.3).set_color(BLUE)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*1, RIGHT*1, UP*1, DOWN*1).set_color(YELLOW).set_opacity(0.6)
        
        # Init positions
        self.place_at_grid(cone, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        plane.move_to(cone.get_center())
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        # Parabola transition
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT, about_point=cone.get_center()))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        # Hyperbola transition
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT, about_point=cone.get_center()))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Dandelin spheres connect 3D cones to 2D geometry.", 
            "They reveal the foci as the conic DNA.", 
            "Geometry and algebra unite through these spheres."
        ])
        
        # Define shapes
        c1 = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=BLUE)
        c2 = Hyperbola(eccentricity=2, color=RED) if hasattr(globals(), 'Hyperbola') else ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([2 * np.cosh(t), np.sinh(t), 0]), t_range=[-2, 2], color=RED)
        c3 = Parabola(a=0.5, color=GREEN) if hasattr(globals(), 'Parabola') else ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5 * t**2, 0]), t_range=[-1, 1], color=GREEN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c1, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(c2, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(c3, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(
            FadeIn(c1), FadeIn(c2), FadeIn(c3),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            Indicate(c1), Indicate(c2), Indicate(c3),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            c1.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            c2.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            c3.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Unlocking Conic Sections
outline.target_audience: High school students or undergraduate mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Anatomy of a Cone and Plane
sections.content: Briefly introduce the 'Double Napped Cone' (two cones meeting at a vertex) and a slicing plane. Establish the concept that the angle of the plane relative to the cone's axis determines the shape of the intersection.
sections.example: Visualizing a laser pointer beam hitting a flat surface at different angles to create circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

sections.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Define the Dandelin Spheres: spheres placed inside the cone that are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the slicing plane (at a single point). These points are the 'Foci' of the conic section.
sections.example: Imagine a 'magic marble' trapped inside a funnel, perfectly touching the cone's surface and a glass sheet covering the funnel.

sections.title: Visual Proof: The Ellipse Case
sections.content: Explain that the distance from any point on the ellipse to the two focal points (the tangency points of the two spheres) is constant. This bridges the geometric intersection with the algebraic definition of an ellipse.
sections.example: Using a diagram showing a 'Planet' (point on the ellipse) orbiting two 'Gravity Anchors' (the foci) where the sum of distances remains constant.

sections.title: Generalization to Parabola and Hyperbola
sections.content: Explain how changing the plane's slope forces one sphere to move to infinity (parabola) or move to the other nap of the cone (hyperbola). Emphasize that the tangency point logic holds for all three shapes.
sections.example: An animation showing a satellite (the plane) changing its trajectory around a planet, transitioning from a circular orbit to a parabolic escape path.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the core takeaway: Dandelin spheres provide the elegant link between 3D spatial geometry (cones) and 2D locus definitions (foci).
sections.example: A final visual overlay showing the 'Glow' of the tangency points on the plane, highlighting that the Foci are the 'secret DNA' of every conic section.
